import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 596

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/596](https://www.erdosproblems.com/596)
- [Er87] Erdős, *Some of my favourite problems in various branches of combinatorics*,
  *Mat. Lapok* 1987.
- [NeRo75] Nešetřil and Rödl, *The Ramsey property for graphs with forbidden complete
  subgraphs*, *J. Combin. Theory* B **20** (1976), 243--249.
-/

open SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos596

/--
**Erdős Problem 596** (Erdős–Hajnal, [Er87]). For which graph pairs $(G_1, G_2)$ is it
true that

  (1) for every $n \geq 1$ there is a graph $H$ without a $G_1$ such that any
      $n$-colouring of $H$'s edges contains a monochromatic $G_2$, and yet
  (2) for every graph $H$ without a $G_1$ there is an $\aleph_0$-colouring of $H$'s edges
      with no monochromatic $G_2$?

Erdős and Hajnal originally conjectured that no such pair exists; but $(C_4, C_6)$
witnesses it (Nešetřil–Rödl + Erdős–Hajnal). The full question is to characterise the
class of all such pairs, recorded here as `answer(sorry)`.

See Problem 595 for the specific case $(G_1, G_2) = (K_4, K_3)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_596 :
    ∀ {U₁ U₂ : Type} (G₁ : SimpleGraph U₁) (G₂ : SimpleGraph U₂),
      IsErdosHajnalExceptional G₁ G₂ ↔
      (answer(sorry) : ∀ {U₁ U₂ : Type}, SimpleGraph U₁ → SimpleGraph U₂ → Prop) G₁ G₂ := by
  sorry

/-- Erdős–Hajnal exceptional pairs exist — recorded as a known direction of `erdos_596`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_596.variants.exists_exceptional :
    ∃ (U₁ U₂ : Type) (G₁ : SimpleGraph U₁) (G₂ : SimpleGraph U₂),
      IsErdosHajnalExceptional G₁ G₂ := by
  sorry

/-- Every $C_4$-free graph is a countable union of trees (Erdős–Hajnal [Er87]); trees are
acyclic, hence $C_6$-free, giving the countable Ramsey escape for $(C_4, C_6)$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_596.variants.C4_free_countable_escape :
    HasCountableRamseyEscape (cycleGraph 4) (cycleGraph 6) := by
  sorry

/-- Nešetřil–Rödl [NeRo75]: for every $n \geq 1$ there is a $C_4$-free graph whose edges
cannot be $n$-coloured without a monochromatic $C_6$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_596.variants.C4_C6_finite_ramsey :
    HasFiniteRamseyProperty (cycleGraph 4) (cycleGraph 6) := by
  sorry

/-- The pair $(C_4, C_6)$ is Erdős–Hajnal exceptional; combines `C4_C6_finite_ramsey` and
`C4_free_countable_escape`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_596.variants.C4_C6_is_exceptional :
    IsErdosHajnalExceptional (cycleGraph 4) (cycleGraph 6) :=
  ⟨erdos_596.variants.C4_C6_finite_ramsey, erdos_596.variants.C4_free_countable_escape⟩

/-- The original Erdős–Hajnal conjecture (that no exceptional pair exists) is **false** —
witnessed by $(C_4, C_6)$ via `C4_C6_is_exceptional`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_596.variants.original_conjecture_is_false : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ {U₁ U₂ : Type} (G₁ : SimpleGraph U₁) (G₂ : SimpleGraph U₂),
      ¬IsErdosHajnalExceptional G₁ G₂ := by
  sorry

/-- Whether $(K_4, K_3)$ is Erdős–Hajnal exceptional is precisely the content of
Erdős Problem 595. The finite Ramsey property holds (Folkman 1970, Nešetřil–Rödl
[NeRo75]); the open part is whether every $K_4$-free graph is a countable union of
triangle-free graphs. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_596.variants.K4_K3_exceptional_iff : answer(sorry) ↔
    IsErdosHajnalExceptional (completeGraph (Fin 4)) (completeGraph (Fin 3)) := by
  sorry

/-- Folkman 1970 / Nešetřil–Rödl [NeRo75]: for every $n \geq 1$ there is a $K_4$-free
graph whose edges cannot be $n$-coloured without a monochromatic triangle. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_596.variants.K4_K3_finite_ramsey :
    HasFiniteRamseyProperty (completeGraph (Fin 4)) (completeGraph (Fin 3)) := by
  sorry

/- ## Sanity checks -/

/-- The empty graph on `Fin 0` is `Free` of any nontrivial subgraph (vacuous). This is the
simplest non-trivial witness to `G₁.Free H` appearing in `HasFiniteRamseyProperty`. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_596.test.empty_is_free :
    (cycleGraph 4).Free (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 0)) :=
  fun ⟨f⟩ => Fin.elim0 (f.toEmbedding 0)

end Erdos596

findings.description: The bibliography entry [Er87] (lines 24–25) gives the wrong title and publication: “Some of my favourite problems in various branches of combinatorics”, Mat. Lapok, 1987. The cited source for this problem is instead Erdős’s “Some problems on finite and infinite graphs”. The mathematical statements agree with the actual source.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/bibs/Er87 identifies “Some problems on finite and infinite graphs”, Logic and combinatorics (Arcata, Calif., 1985) (1987), 223–228. Section 5, pp. 224–225, of https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1987-28.pdf contains the graph-pair question, the (C4,C6) counterexample, and the countable-union-of-trees result.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace [Er87] with: Erdős, P., “Some problems on finite and infinite graphs”, Logic and combinatorics (Arcata, Calif., 1985), Contemporary Mathematics 65 (1987), 223–228; optionally cite §5 explicitly.

findings.description: The docstring attributes the C4-free/C6 Ramsey construction to [NeRo75], whose bibliography entry names the 1976 paper on forbidden complete subgraphs. The original source identifies a different Nešetřil–Rödl paper for this construction: their 1987 Transactions of the AMS paper on Steiner systems. This is a reference error, not an error in the Lean statement or its solved status.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős, “Some problems on finite and infinite graphs”, §5, p. 225 (https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1987-28.pdf), states the C4-free/C6 result and says the Nešetřil–Rödl paper will appear in Transactions of the AMS. Nešetřil–Rödl, “Strong Ramsey theorems for Steiner systems”, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 303 (1987), 183–192, Theorem 6.3, states that the class of bipartite C4-free graphs has the edge partition property; applying it to C6 gives this declaration. See https://www.ams.org/journals/tran/1987-303-01/S0002-9947-1987-0896015-8/S0002-9947-1987-0896015-8.pdf.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the 1987 Steiner-systems paper to the bibliography and cite its Theorem 6.3 in this docstring. The 1976 clique-Ramsey reference can remain for the K4/K3 material.

reformulations.difference: Problem 595’s finite result is phrased as a K4-free graph that is not a union of n triangle-free graphs. Lean instead requires a monochromatic triangle in every partition of its edges into n colour classes.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A triangle-free edge partition is a triangle-free cover. Conversely, refine any indexed cover by replacing its ith graph with the edges not already assigned to earlier graphs. This preserves the union and triangle-freeness and makes the classes disjoint. Also, (completeGraph (Fin 3)).Free H is equivalent to H.CliqueFree 3. Negating the existence of such a cover therefore gives exactly the Lean Ramsey condition. The generic finite-cover equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean without sorry dependencies.

reformulations.difference: Lean packages the question using exceptional pairs, including a known finite-Ramsey condition, rather than directly using the universal countable-union-of-triangle-free-graphs formulation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The known K4/K3 finite-Ramsey property makes exceptionality equivalent to countable Ramsey escape. Countable covers can be refined into disjoint colour classes, and clique-freeness agrees with absence of the corresponding complete-graph copy. Thus exceptionality is equivalent to every K4-free graph being a countable union of triangle-free graphs. I also proved that this is equivalent to the negation of Problem 595’s infinite-counterexample proposition: finite graphs, indeed all countable graphs, have a countable star cover. These equivalences were proved in Lean with the known finite-Ramsey theorem as an explicit hypothesis. The answer polarity is consistent with Problem 596’s own question about whether the pair is exceptional; its positive answer would be a negative answer to Problem 595.

review.notes: Checked all nine declarations and the shared predicates. No mathematical misformalization or stale status was found; both findings concern references only. Scratch checks are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/equivalences.lean. They verify ordinary rather than induced containment, satisfiability of colour partitions, zero/one-colour and empty-graph boundaries, nontriviality of the classification answer, and the relevant cover/colouring equivalences. Computed the named graphs’ edge counts and tested small containment instances. The equivalence proofs have no sorryAx dependencies. The 1976 JCTB full text was inaccessible; the C4/C6 result and its attribution were independently verified in Erdős’s original §5 and Nešetřil–Rödl’s 1987 Theorem 6.3. No repository files were edited.
